population.note: FICTIONAL. US adults ≈276M. Current users: 32.3% ≈ 89.1M, up 3.8 pts. Ever used: 45.0% ≈ 124.2M, up 5.0 pts against a 6.8-pt limit. Never used: ≈151.8M. Used and off now: 45.0 − 32.3 = 12.7 pts ≈ 35.1M. Cycling, in one line: ≈16.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course, and ≈5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (16.5 + 5.0)/45.0 ≈ 47.8%. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. The off-now share grew mainly because of medically advised pauses (bone pause, the new CMS strength-screen pause, NAION workups), tenure-gate separations and price exits, not because of rejection. Age check: 18–29: 18% × 52M = 9.4M; 30–49: 36.8% × 92M = 33.9M; 50–64: 47.5% × 62M = 29.5M; 65+: 23.5% × 70M = 16.5M. Total ≈ 89.1M = 32.3%. The 65+ band grew only 2.5 pts (21 → 23.5) because the 2035 sarcopenia warning and the Nov 2035 CMS functional screen put roughly one in four older ever-users on a pause at any given time. Income thirds average (35 + 33 + 29)/3 ≈ 32.3. Bottom-third growth is again mostly imports (≈8.9M imported or counterfeit users, up from 7.1M) and Medicaid volume in the 31 states plus DC. Pediatric: 1.1% of ≈73M ≈ 800k, mostly adolescents 12+. Growth slowed after the 2035 adolescent bone-accrual readout. About two in five children live with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it, and school nurses now see adolescent 'pause letters'.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory terms of the permanent Part D obesity benefit are unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Medicare pays 18.3% of fills, ≈16.3M users (≈14.9M aged 65+ and ≈1.4M disabled under-65): ≈7.0M for diabetes and ≈9.3M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: 9.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $22.2B gross. Beneficiaries pay 9.3M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.6B, leaving ≈$16.6B for the program. All Medicare incretin fills: 16.3M × $199 × 12 ≈ $38.9B gross. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC use the 90% match and the continuation standard. Medicaid pays 14.7% of fills, ≈13.1M users × $199 × 12 ≈ $31.3B gross before supplemental rebates. The Nov 2035 CMS amendment adds a functional-strength screen for long-term 65+ users. It does not change who pays.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 120+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic oral semaglutide and the first Indian 50 mg-equivalent tablets. The Telangana first-filer plant is still under US import alert. China: generic semaglutide, tirzepatide copies, and 'research' retatrutide vials and tablets. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, Egypt and now Vietnam also have generics. US: the mid-2035 contingent date for rival filers passed with no launch, because a July 2035 district-court injunction froze FDA's forfeiture ruling on the first filer's parked 180-day exclusivity pending appeal.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. Direct-portal prices did not move in either year: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $249–329; Wegovy pill 50 mg $299; oral starters (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) $149–150; retatrutide $449 direct and $1,649 list; amycretin $499; MariTide $549/month-equivalent. PBM net is ≈$195–215. Payer mix of ≈89.1M users: commercial 37.0% (33.0M); Medicare 18.3% (16.3M); Medicaid 14.7% (13.1M); cash/direct 20.0% (17.8M, including ≈4.2M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers, down from 4.6M); imported/counterfeit 10.0% (8.9M). Sum = 100% = 89.1M. Employer coverage holds at 64%. About 88% of covering plans are gated, ≈40% of gated plans add tenure gates, and after the Jan 2036 tri-agency guidance a growing minority price premiums off pharmacy PDC as well as kiosk weight. Routes: ≈42% of users are on daily orals, up from ≈36%. The 503B exclusion and 503A injunction stand.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, incl. 7.2 mg)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (≈4.2M subscribers, now sold with 'weekend mode' holiday schedules)
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial fully enrolled, readout 2037)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices, now bundled with strength coaching
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care, slowed after the 2035 bone readout
gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users
deliberate dose holidays and step-downs to starter doses for mood, sex and pleasure (practice, not an indication)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class and no new indication. The survodutide MASH sNDA, under review at the start, received a complete response letter in Sep 2035 that asks for 18-month histology outcomes. Bimagrumab combinations read out positive phase 3 lean-mass data in Mar 2036 (lean share of loss ≈10% versus ≈35% on tirzepatide alone). No BLA has been filed, and Lilly guides to a 2037 filing, so nothing can reach market before 2038. This is the most-watched asset in the field because of the muscle-bone wave. Lilly's next-generation orals entered phase 3 in 2035 and are unfiled. US generic semaglutide is still parked behind the forfeiture litigation. Incretin market ≈$215B in 2036. US ≈$192B: ≈80.2M paying users (89.1M − 8.9M imports) × ≈$200 average net × 12 ≈ $192.5B. Ex-US ≈$22B and eroding as generics spread. The US increase is all volume, with net price flat.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Dose holidays add a new wave of 'restart nausea' on Mondays.
Absolute numbers keep rising with high-dose regimens and the larger long-term population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray-market dosing errors still confound reporting.

Recognised as a population problem. The Feb 2035 NIH–CMS linked-claims analysis finds ≈2.3M long-term users aged 65+ meeting sarcopenia criteria (up from ≈1.6M) and ≈0.9M aged 50–64. Lean mass is 30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. Grip-strength decline is measurable after 18 months in untrained users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Feb 2035: class Warnings and Precautions language on muscle loss across all GLP-1 products, with recommended baseline and periodic functional assessment. Nov 2035: CMS adds a grip-strength and chair-stand screen to six-monthly verification for 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. A failed screen requires either logged enrolment in prescribed resistance training or a 90-day pause.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.8M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.8M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 18,500 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. Vertebral fractures concentrate among cycling postmenopausal women 50–64. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks as mobile capacity expands.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Folded into the Feb 2035 class Warnings and Precautions update. Bone endpoints required in all filings. CMS bone-pause code retained and now triggered by the functional screen. Private gated plans are still not bound by it. DOJ civil case against Novo settled in 2036 with no admission.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Relative risk ≈1.7. At ~4 per 100,000 baseline across ≈89M users, roughly 2,500 excess cases a year, mostly partial permanent vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions (May 2034) retained; not boxed. MDL consolidated in 2035.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The 2032 retatrutide figure (~12% vs ~5%) is replicated in a 2035 Danish registry analysis. The Mar 2036 NHIS supplement finds 31% of current users took a deliberate dose holiday or step-down in the past year, with 'feeling flat' the most-cited reason after GI effects. There is still no randomised low-dose measurement; an NIH-funded trial is enrolling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FTC consent orders stand. FDA declines a label change pending randomised data.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mandated strength-screen pauses, tenure-gate separations and holidays add new stop types to the existing ones.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare. The Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver in Aug 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12, vitamin D and calcium insufficiency are common among high-loss older and gray-market users. It is now cited as a contributor to sarcopenia.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screens for it. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use, and holidays create a new micro-cycling pattern that no one has studied.
New entry, split out from the long-horizon line. The 2035 adolescent trial readout shows a mean BMD z-score ≈0.3 lower than comparators at 2 years. Fracture significance is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Feb 2035: pediatric labelling recommends DEXA at baseline and at 2 years. AAP guidance favours structured pauses through peak accrual.

safety_ledger.effect: Functional decline and loss of independence in long-term older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Medicare Advantage claims show higher rates of new home-health episodes and assisted-device use in untrained 65+ users after 3+ years, partly confounded by frailty at baseline.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Cited in the CMS functional-screen rule; no label action.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.9M import users. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are up a further ~25% since 2034. There has been no cluster on the scale of the 2033 contamination; infections are sporadic.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA import alerts extended to seven exporters. Safe Pens bill still stalled. Individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pressed fakes are now the majority of seized gray product by unit, with 0–300% of labelled content. Hypoglycaemia in insulin users is the main harm.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated among 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Monocular vision loss is a minority cofactor.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening in the Part D counselling visit, now paired with the strength screen.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging. Joint Endocrine Society and American Geriatrics Society guidance (2035) names it 'cycling sarcopenic obesity'. It concentrates in over-50s cut off by gating, tenure gaps and pauses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint professional guidance; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting heart rate up several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

food_and_beverage.state: With about a third of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume keeps falling ~3–4% a year and confectionery ~4%. The muscle-bone wave makes protein the main growth category. Branded high-leucine dairy, 'grip' shakes and fortified bone lines are now in every supermarket chain. The price split widens. Premium whey sells to coached users. Dollar stores sell soy-protein value packs and calorie-dense 'pause packs' to people on mandated pauses or cycling off.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits decline; beer down. Holiday weekends produce a measurable Friday–Saturday bump in on-premise drinking that distributors now plan around. Tobacco and vape keep falling.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, spend per cover still ~10% below 2028. Gram-priced protein bowls are standard. Weekend 'holiday menus' with full portions and dessert flights spread in high-uptake suburbs. Value buffets in non-expansion rural states keep their partial recovery.

apparel.state: The 'structured' and 'cycle' split is industry standard. Premium brands cut for trained shoulders and offer free DEXA-matched tailoring. Discount 'cycle' ranges add adaptive closures for older customers with weak grip. The mid-market keeps shrinking.

fitness.state: The fastest-growing category this step. After the CMS screen, Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' enrolment roughly doubles. Strip-mall DEXA-and-strength chains go national, and connected dynamometers that log to plan portals ship in the millions. The binding constraint is still trainers qualified for older lifters, and wait lists in Sun Belt suburbs run 6–10 weeks.

insurance.state: Employer coverage holds at 64%. Gating reaches ~88% of covering plans, ~40% with tenure gates. After the Jan 2036 tri-agency guidance, premium tiers can key off pharmacy PDC and kiosk weight within the 30% surcharge cap. Pharmacy trend ~+6%, all volume. Fracture, fall and home-health costs keep landing on Part A and MA medical budgets. Long-term-care insurers begin asking about incretin duration and resistance-training history.

pharma.state: Volume up ~14% over two years with net price flat. Lilly leads on retatrutide, tirzepatide and Foundayo, Amgen grows MariTide, and Novo's 50 mg pill takes most oral switching. Valuations now hinge on lean-mass preservation (bimagrumab). Indian and Chinese makers dominate abroad and in the parcel trade.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, now read through muscle. Thinness is near-universal among users and tells you little. Grip, posture and shoulder shape tell you a lot. 'Lift calluses', a DEXA-verified badge and steady weight signal a coached top-third regimen. A soft, narrow-shouldered 'pill body' signals the middle. The forward stoop, thin forearms and regained middle of a mandated pause or a parcel pen signal the bottom.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates converge (29% bottom third against 35% top) and bodies diverge further. In metro Atlanta, Buckhead and Alpharetta strength studios run 'lean-mass guarantee' packages. In Clayton County, Medicaid users wait on prescribed-lifting slots and import users have no screen at all. Women 50–64 remain the most visibly sorted group. Those coached through menopause keep bone and muscle, and those who cycled carry the vertebral-fracture tail. 'She lifts' has become shorthand for 'she has good insurance'.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals are the norm among users. The new ritual is the holiday meal: Friday or Saturday dinners where users skip a dose and eat fully, so restaurants and church suppers in Atlanta and Houston fill on weekends. Off and cycling working-class families keep the full-table Sunday.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: A major dating app launched a 'scan-verified' badge in 2036, which users treat as a pay stub. Profiles list holiday schedules ('weekends off'). Couples coordinate holidays the way they once coordinated vacations.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Managed during the week and permitted on holidays. Appetite is something you schedule. The backlash coalition is stable in size. Its argument has moved from pen poverty to 'they sold us thin and took our legs', which resonates with seniors' groups.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. ≈9M Americans are on top-dose triple or dual regimens. At the 12% vs 5% registry figure, that implies ~630k excess clinically meaningful anhedonia cases if the association is causal. ≈4.2M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers remain unmeasured. The NHIS 2036 supplement finds 31% of ≈89M current users (≈27.6M) took a deliberate holiday or step-down in the past year, and about 40% of those cited feeling flat. 'Fill-compliant holidays' (keep filling, skip doses) are widespread because PDC counts fills, not doses taken.
interior_life.framing: Complaint, not feature. 'The grey' is a dinner-party subject, a late-night joke and a reason people give for a holiday weekend. Brands that sold calm now sell 'weekend mode' and 'flex dosing'. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. Everyone else says 'grey weeks'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers still reimburse 'focus' through lifestyle accounts, but uptake has fallen and some HR departments quietly drop it after 'grey' complaints in engagement surveys. Tenure gates keep warehouse and call-centre workers in place. 'Holiday Fridays' show up as slower Mondays with restart nausea. Unions now bargain over whether a mandated strength-screen pause counts against plan gating.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' label now describes the sound of a whole decade. A memoir genre about 'coming out of the grey' sells well. Comedy tours run 'holiday weekend' bits. Clubs and live venues in Nashville and Austin book Friday–Saturday heavy and dark midweek.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists routinely prescribe coordinated holidays. Couples on mismatched schedules (one on a weekly pen, one on a daily pill) report out-of-phase desire. 'Restart packs' with anti-nausea medication and electrolytes sit next to condoms in pharmacies.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The complaint went political. Senators from both parties wrote to FDA demanding a randomised low-dose study, and NIH funded one. Seniors' groups campaign on 'strength, not just scales' and against the CMS screen pausing their drug. Price and import remain the core issue, and the Safe Pens bill is still stalled.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and cautious. It upgraded class muscle and bone warnings, added adolescent bone-monitoring language, issued a CRL on the survodutide MASH sNDA, and declined a blunting label without randomised data. It still brings no individual prosecutions, and Congress has passed neither an importation law nor an authentication law.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged in who pays. The Part D obesity benefit stays at $199 with a $50 copay, and 31 states plus DC keep the 90% Medicaid match. There is no individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning deepened. The Nov 2035 CMS final rule adds a grip-strength and chair-stand screen at six-monthly verification for 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. A failed screen requires logged enrolment in prescribed resistance training (connected dynamometer or gym check-ins) or a 90-day pause. ≥80% PDC, verified weights and the two-miss rule are unchanged. The Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver in Aug 2035, and Arkansas's 12-month rule stands. The Jan 2036 HHS/DOL/Treasury wellness guidance confirms that pharmacy PDC and verified kiosk weights qualify as outcome-based wellness criteria within the 30% surcharge cap. Kiosk, scale, pharmacy and now dynamometer data feed both public eligibility and private premiums.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and large fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks. Some warehouse employers add 'lift capacity' re-certification for medicated workers over 55 after injury claims. Army accession policy is still contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese API and Indian finished product supply the world and the 8.9M-user US gray market. Section 232 tariffs remain. The Telangana import alert and the US forfeiture litigation are standing irritants in US–India trade talks.

events.event: FDA adds class-wide warnings on muscle loss and bone density to every GLP-1 drug label after an NIH–CMS analysis finds about 2.3 million long-term users over 65 meet sarcopenia criteria and about 18,500 excess hip fractures occur a year. An adolescent trial readout shows lower bone accrual, and pediatric labels now recommend scans

The mid-2035 date for rival generic semaglutide passes with no launch after a federal district court enjoins FDA's ruling that the first filer forfeited its 180-day exclusivity. Novo and Lilly hold direct-portal prices flat for a second year, and the cheapest maintenance pen stays at $249

CMS finalises a rule requiring grip-strength and chair-stand tests for Medicare and Medicaid incretin users over 65 with more than two years of use. Those who fail must log prescribed resistance training or take a 90-day pause. Seniors' groups call it 'a strength test for your prescription'

Federal labor, health and treasury agencies issue guidance confirming that employers may tie up to 30% of premiums to pharmacy refill adherence and verified kiosk weights. Within weeks, two national benefits administrators add adherence tiers to their 'metabolic tier' plans

A federal health survey finds 31% of Americans on incretin drugs took a deliberate dose holiday in the past year, many citing 'the grey'. The largest 'calm' subscription brand launches a 'weekend mode' schedule, and senators press FDA for a randomised low-dose study

A Federal Reserve working paper documents a 'lean-mass gap': DEXA-measured muscle tracks household income among incretin users more closely than weight does. The same month, a major dating app launches a 'scan-verified' badge

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide is parked again, now behind forfeiture litigation with no date, and prices have stalled at 2034 levels. ≈8.9M Americans rely on imported pens and pressed pills, and the Safe Pens bill remains stalled.

Conditioning now runs on fills, weights and grip strength. Because PDC counts fills, not doses, ≈27M holiday-takers are 'adherent' on paper. Employers and CMS are starting to ask for dose-level data such as smart-pen logs and pill-bottle sensors, which would make the holidays users depend on visible to payers.

The muscle-bone wave falls on Part A, Medicare Advantage and long-term care (≈18,500 excess hip fractures a year, new home-health episodes), while the drug sits in Part D at a fixed $199. The only lean-sparing fix, bimagrumab, is unfiled until 2037, and the CMS screen pauses the people who can least afford regain.
'The grey' is a mainstream complaint with no randomised data. FTC still permits 'calm' and 'focus' marketing to ≈4.2M subscribers. The NIH trial will not read out before 2038.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The same 31 states plus DC use the 90% Medicaid match and the CMS continuation standard; no state joined or left.
The FTC consent orders stand: no 'anxiety treatment' claims, while 'calm' and 'focus' marketing is permitted.

prose.headline: Show Me Your Grip: In 2036, Everyone's Thin and Your Muscle Says What You Earn
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 nearly one American adult in three is on an incretin drug, about eighty-nine million people. Another thirty-five million have used one and are off it for now, most of them only temporarily. Being thin has stopped meaning anything in particular. What people read now is muscle. A firm handshake, a straight back, forearms that have clearly lifted something heavy: these mean a coached regimen, an annual scan, a trainer who knows bone. A narrow, soft frame means the daily pill on a gated employer plan. A forward stoop over a regained middle means a pause you did not choose, or a pen that came in the mail from Hyderabad. A Federal Reserve paper put numbers to it in June. Among users, muscle mass tracks household income more closely than weight does. A dating app added a scan-verified badge the same month, and users treat it as a pay stub.

The drugs are the same ones as two years ago. Nothing new reached the market, and no new indication was approved. Prices stopped falling and stayed where the 2033 price increase left them. Generic semaglutide was due in mid-2035. Instead a federal judge froze the FDA's ruling that the first filer had lost its exclusive right to launch, and the whole queue is stuck again with no date. The cheapest maintenance pen is still $249. The starter pills are still $149. Medicare still pays its statutory $199. Almost nine million people buy abroad, increasingly as pressed tablets of uncertain strength.

What changed is the cost to the body. In February 2035 an analysis linking NIH and Medicare data found about 2.3 million long-term users over sixty-five meeting the clinical definition of sarcopenia, and about eighteen thousand excess hip fractures a year. The FDA put muscle and bone warnings on every label. A trial in adolescents found slower bone growth, and children's prescriptions now come with scans. Medicare's answer was to set a test. Since late 2035, older long-term users have to squeeze a dynamometer and stand up from a chair five times at each six-monthly check. Those who fail must log supervised lifting or take a ninety-day pause. Gyms that specialise in older lifters have waiting lists. Seniors' groups call it a strength test for your prescription.

Employers had a template to copy. A January 2036 federal guidance confirmed that pharmacy refill records and kiosk weights can set up to thirty percent of an employee's premium. Most plans that cover the drug were already gated by weight loss, and about two in five also require a year's tenure. Workers in warehouses and call centres still talk about waiting to vest.

The gauges have a gap. They measure fills, not swallowed doses. A March federal survey found that thirty-one percent of users took a deliberate holiday in the past year: skipping the pill on weekends, stepping down to a starter dose, letting a weekly shot slide. The most common reason after nausea was the grey, the flatness that the 'calm' brands once sold as a feature. Those brands now sell a 'weekend mode'. Friday dinners are full again, and Monday mornings bring restart nausea. Senators asked for a randomised trial of low doses. It is enrolling and will not report for years.

None of this looks like a crisis. Restaurants are busy on weekends. Protein shakes fill the dollar-store shelves. The drug is cheap at Medicare's counter and expensive at nobody's, as long as you have a job you have held for a year. The fractures are billed to a part of Medicare that does not pay for the drug. The only molecule that seems to spare muscle will not be filed until 2037.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorraine Bell is sixty-one and runs the cafeteria at a middle school in Clayton County. At 5:40 she stands on the pharmacy kiosk at the Kroger on Tara Boulevard, shoes off, badge scanned. 211.4. The screen turns green. The district plan counts the green, and so does the refill clock on her fifty-milligram pill, which she has been filling on time all year.

She didn't take one Saturday or Sunday. She never does.

At work she plates turkey-and-egg bowls, thirty grams each, for children who mostly don't finish them. One eighth-grader hands her a folded note from the nurse: pause per bone scan, no medication on file. Lorraine files it with the allergy cards.

At three she drives to her mother's clinic in Riverdale. Mama is eighty-four and has been on Medicare's plan since the benefit started. Today the aide hands her the grip meter and counts the chair stands. Three. She needed five. The aide types, apologises, and prints a sheet listing two gyms with older-lifter slots. The nearer one's wait is nine weeks. The other option is a ninety-day pause. Mama chooses the pause. Lorraine is the one who looks away.

Dinner is her daughter Keisha's Friday thing: a Buckhead place with a 'holiday menu', short ribs and a dessert flight. Keisha shows her a dating profile with a little blue shield. Scan-verified, she says. He's a lawyer.

Lorraine orders the short ribs. Her hand feels small around the fork. Tomorrow she won't take the pill, and on Monday she'll be sick.

least_plausible_claims.quote: A Federal Reserve working paper documents a 'lean-mass gap': DEXA-measured muscle tracks household income among incretin users more closely than weight does.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: no source of DEXA data is shown for a population-wide comparison that would have to include 8.9M import users with no clinical contact. A Fed working paper is a convenient vehicle for the stratification driver, and the finding is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Tomorrow she won't take the pill, and on Monday she'll be sick.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: this contradicts the earlier line "She didn't take one Saturday or Sunday. She never does." The same protagonist both skips weekend doses and never does, so the day-in-the-life disagrees with itself.

least_plausible_claims.quote: connected dynamometers that log to plan portals ship in the millions
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: the CMS screen only took effect in Nov 2035 and applies to 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Millions of connected devices shipping within about a year is asserted with no fail-rate or procurement chain behind it.

rationale.badness: Measured against 2026, this world keeps every harm it inherited and deepens them. About 32% of adults are on the drug, ≈18,500 excess hip fractures a year, 2.3M older users with sarcopenia, and ≈8.9M people on imported or pressed-pill product. Coverage is conditioned on kiosk weights, PDC, grip tests and tenure gates, and body shape has become an income marker (body_and_culture, state/conditioning). Autonomy and inequality are the worst dimensions. The blunting question stays unmeasured but widely felt, so epistemic harm is moderate. The world is a society many present-day readers would refuse, though it is not collapse.
